quote: When it was learned, long before Wainer was born, that the electronic brains could be inserted within the human brain and connected with the main neural paths, there was no one who did not think it was the greatest discovery of all time.
claim_description: Electronic computers implanted in the human brain and linked to its neural pathways.
concept_description: An electronic device implanted in or joined to the human body or brain to restore or extend senses, memory or ability.
milestone_summary: Hochmair's multichannel cochlear implant was first implanted in a person in Vienna in December 1977; Clark's followed in 1978 and was commercialized as Nucleus.

quote: 'He responds to an auditory mechanism very similar in principle to an electric eye.
claim_description: A robot that hears and responds to spoken commands via an electronic auditory sensor.
concept_description: A machine that recognizes spoken words and carries out spoken commands, such as voice-operated doors or computers.
milestone_summary: Threshold Technology (Delran/Cinnaminson, NJ) brought out the VIP-100 isolated-word recognizer and had voice-input terminals working in industrial, government and military 'real-world' use from late 1972.

quote: He fed it into the photoelectric tracer, marked in the necessary coding for an unlimited file search: "Any person resembling this description in any way: any information on—"
claim_description: An automated electronic archive can search for people by a photograph on a card and a coded description.
concept_description: Cameras and computers that identify people by matching their faces against stored images.
milestone_summary: By 1994 facial-recognition biometric products had reached the marketplace (access control); the DMV offices of West Virginia and New Mexico followed, using automated face recognition against duplicate licences after the 1993 FERET test.

quote: He plugged in the machine, and put on the reel. It was his father's voice.
claim_description: A sleep-instructor device that teaches languages, history and other knowledge to a sleeping person via audio reels.
concept_description: Teaching people while they sleep or are hypnotized by playing recorded lessons.
milestone_summary: Zust et al. (University of Bern) played recorded pseudoword/German word pairs to young adults in slow-wave sleep and found they had formed and kept new word associations that showed up on an implicit test after waking.

quote: these were connected by electric wires with the kitchen of the hotel, and if I would observe the numbers attached to any articles in the bill of fare which I desired, and would touch the corresponding numbers of the knobs before me, my dinner would be ordered on a similar mirror in the kitchen
claim_description: Electric button ordering from the table transmitted to the kitchen, with food delivered up through the table.
concept_description: Controlling a machine by touching a screen or panel, or by hand gestures and gloves read by sensors.
milestone_summary: PLATO IV terminals at the University of Illinois (1972) had a built-in 16x16 infrared touch panel that students used to answer questions in lessons
